title: Blood Routes
dek: 351 people died in 15 days during the 2026 Eid-ul-Fitr rush. Bangladesh's roads kill at six times the official count. The joma incentive system, political shields, and four critical data voids make it structural — not accidental.
summary: A scroll-driven visual investigation into nationwide road crash fatalities in Bangladesh: the Eid holiday surge, the joma economic machine that incentivises racing, the Phoenix rebrand pattern, and four data voids the government holds but refuses to publish.
key_findings: During the 15-day Eid-ul-Fitr 2026 travel period, 351 people were killed — averaging 23 deaths per day during the holiday rush.
The WHO-modelled road death estimate (~31,578/year) is 5.8× higher than the BRTA official count (5,480) — a gap maintained by deliberate policy, not technical incapacity.

The joma (daily deposit) system forces bus drivers to race for passengers under a guaranteed-income model that protects owners and transfers all lethal risk to drivers and pedestrians, 47% of Dhaka victims.
